figures.finding: Mauritius's Film Rebate Scheme, run by the Economic Development Board under the EDB (Film Rebate Scheme) Regulation 2018, refunds 30% of qualifying production expenditure incurred in Mauritius, and up to 40% for a feature spending at least USD 1,000,000 or a drama series spending at least USD 150,000 an episode; the 30% band needs a minimum of USD 100,000 for a foreign feature (USD 50,000 local) and USD 20,000 an episode for TV drama; local and foreign producers qualify.

value.name: Film Rebate Scheme (EDB Mauritius)
value.regulation: Economic Development Board (Film Rebate Scheme) Regulation 2018
value.base: Qualifying Production Expenditure (QPE) incurred in Mauritius

figures.applies: Mauritius; local and foreign producers; guideline dated 31 January 2020, still linked from the EDB's Creative Industry page on 2026-11-01.

sources.said: The Film Rebate Scheme, implemented in 2013, was a first step towards the development of a cinematographic industry in Mauritius, under which film makers benefit of 30% rebate on all the qualifying expenditures incurred in Mauritius. A new band of 40% rebate has been introduced in the National Budget 2016-2017 on all qualifying expenditures incurred by a feature film in Mauritius (Minimum QPE of USD 1,000,000). This new band has been extended, through the National Budget 2018-2019, to high-end Television Series (Minimum QPE of USD 150,000). The Regulation is cited as the Economic Development Board (Film Rebate Scheme) Regulation 2018. … Category of Production Minimum QPE (USD) Eligible for 30% rebate Foreign Production Local Production Feature film (including animation) 100,000 50,000 Television drama series or single drama 20,000 (per episode) 20,000 Television documentary programme 20,000 20,000

The Film Rebate Scheme is managed by the Economic Development Board. Local and Foreign film producer can benefit from 30% up to 40% of rebate on Qualifying Production Expenditures incurred in Mauritius for a production.

figures.finding: Independent local filmmakers can get a Mauritius Film Development Corporation (MFDC) Film Grant of at most Rs 2 million on an approved project, under the National Resilience Fund, with the EDB and the Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage.

sources.said: Mauritius Film Development Corporation (MFDC) in collaboration with the Economic Development Board (EDB) and the Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage (MACH) has introduced the Mauritius Film Development Corporation (MFDC) Film Grant to support independent local filmmakers to a maximum grant of 2 Million on approved projects.
